For small manufacturers selling into federal contracts, a Made-in-USA or Buy American Act domestic-content claim usually lives in a spreadsheet or a PDF — a self-attestation that a contracting officer has to take mostly on faith. GovChain hash-anchors that provenance record to Polygon instead, so the claim behind a component or product is a tamper-evident record anyone can independently check, not paperwork sitting in a folder.

The same system also watches the federal opportunity feed and scores each incoming notice against a contractor's actual capabilities, attaching a plain-English pursue / monitor / skip call to every score instead of just a keyword match — and from there it can auto-draft a starting capability statement. It also tracks certification status (ISO 9001, AS9100, CMMC) so a renewal deadline doesn't slip past unnoticed.

If your domestic-content claims are still a PDF nobody outside your own team can verify, take a look at what an anchored provenance record changes.

reddit.title: How do you actually document Made-in-USA / BAA domestic-content claims — anchored provenance record, or still a self-attested PDF?
reddit.body:
For federal contracts, a Made-in-USA or Buy American Act domestic-content claim usually just sits in a spreadsheet or a PDF that a contracting officer has to take mostly on faith. I've been working on GovChain, which hash-anchors that provenance record to Polygon instead, so the claim behind a component or product becomes a tamper-evident record anyone can independently check rather than paperwork in a folder.

The same tool also watches the federal opportunity feed and scores incoming notices against a contractor's actual capabilities, attaching a plain-English pursue / monitor / skip call instead of just matching keywords, and can auto-draft a starting capability statement once you decide to pursue something. It also tracks certification status (ISO 9001, AS9100, CMMC) so a renewal doesn't sneak up on you.

Curious how others here handle documenting domestic-content claims today — is anyone actually anchoring or notarizing that record anywhere, or is it still all self-attested paperwork sitting in a shared drive?
